title: The thread in the box

data.source: A toy of this room's own: 2000 seeded threads wandering along a line. No neural network was examined.
data.licence: none needed (generated here from a seed)

prediction: Nothing about a real network is predicted here. The cartoon's arithmetic holds: the thread is never shorter than the distance between its ends, the surplus adds nothing once length and distance are both known, and threads with the same ends can differ in length.
baseline: Ordinary geometry and ordinary regression. For the real question the rivals Phoenix names are behavioural audits, linear probes, sparse-autoencoder features, circuit tracing, generic path length and a generic sequence model given the same activations.
why: Phoenix calls this an open programme and has run no test: the proposed instrument does not yet differ from an event log. The toy shows only that an ends-only account leaves something out, and that the surplus is not a third, independent thing to measure.
phoenix_status: "Status: OPEN RESEARCH PROGRAMME. CRR has not solved the black-box problem." Enquiry P17: SPARK, "not yet declarable"; "no instrument". If CRR only offers a visualisation Phoenix grades it "U2 methodological, not empirical evidence".
